articles.headline: Colts will use Jonathan Taylor more after Seth McGowan injury update
keyFacts: Leading up to the 2026 NFL trade deadline, there wasn't a more talked-about trade than a potential Jonathan Taylor deal.
The Indianapolis Colts didn't budge and kept him through the deadline.
Taylor remained in Indianapolis, and the split workload in the backfield between him and Seth McGowan continued, even after the Colts limited Taylor's work to keep him healthy in case of a trade.
body: Leading up to the 2026 NFL trade deadline, there wasn't a more talked-about trade than a potential Jonathan Taylor deal. The Indianapolis Colts didn't budge and kept him through the deadline.
Taylor remained in Indianapolis, and the split workload in the backfield between him and Seth McGowan continued, even after the Colts limited Taylor's work to keep him healthy in case of a trade.

But now, the Colts are going to need Taylor more than ever. According to ESPN's Stephen Holder, McGowan is going to miss "some time," per head coach Shane Steichen, likely leading to more work for Taylor.
Colts to rely more on Jonathan Taylor after Seth McGowan news
"Steichen says rookie RB Seth McGowan will miss some time in the lineup after his injury Thursday night," Holder reports. "No timeline right now. Probably means bigger workload for Jonathan Taylor."
This is a tough blow for the Colts, who seemed to have found something in McGowan, the rookie running back out of Kentucky.
He had 58 rushing attempts for two touchdowns and 292 yards. He also had six catches on seven targets for 10 yards. But now, he's set to miss some time.

While it's not known if he'll need to land on injured reserve, meaning he'd miss the next four Colts games, it's apparent that McGowan will be out for a little while, at least through the Week 13 bye.
Taylor, who has not had more than 16 rushing attempts since their game against the Minnesota Vikings, might finally be in line for a much larger role out of the backfield going forward.
He hasn't scored a rushing touchdown in the last four weeks, as McGowan has been getting a lot of work in the backfield.

But with the rookie set to miss some time, Taylor is poised for a larger role. He'll play alongside Anthony Richardson Sr., as the Colts waived Daniel Jones following their 26-3 loss on Thursday Night Football to the Houston Texans.

The Colts and Taylor, sitting at 3-8, are going to be facing off against the New York Giants in Week 12, the one team linked to Taylor the most this year. He'll be the bell cow in Indianapolis for the first time in a little while as McGowan sits for some time.

keyFacts: Kirby Smart provided a brief comment on the future of No.

body: Kirby Smart provided a brief comment on the future of No. 1 Georgia's defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann and his potential future as Florida State football's head coach.

Speaking during a Monday, Nov. 23 press conference, the Georgia head coach was asked directly if he's had any conversations with Schumann about his potential move to take over as head coach of the Seminoles (5-6, 3-5 ACC).
His response was brief.
"Schumann has done a fabulous job here, and anything that comes from his success; he has earned every bit of it," Smart said. "But the University of Georgia is focused on Georgia Tech."

Short and sweet from Smart. But despite his avoidance, Schumann remains the Seminoles' frontrunner for the vacant head coach role, which became available after Mike Norvell was fired Nov. 1. The university and Schumann have met to discuss the role, and multiple reports suggest that the two parties are close to an agreement.

He has emerged as the lead candidate early in the Seminoles search, and his connection with now FSU athletic director Jeff Purinton could be playing a key role. Schumann and Purinton crossed paths at Alabama when Schumann started working as an undergraduate assistant under Nick Saban before he eventually followed Smart to Georgia.

Schumann has earned a reputation for being an elite recruiter and developer of talent with the Bulldogs. One such example of that is linebacker Justin Williams. The former 5-star prospect who Schumann recruited to Athens spoke about the potential departure of his defensive coordinator when asked.

"I know nothing about it. I mean, I'm really happy for him, whatever he chooses to do. He's a great coach, great individual," Williams said. "I see him like a father figure to me. He's a great guy. So whatever he wants to do, I'm happy for him."

No public announcements have been made about the future of Schumann, but he remains the frontrunner in the Seminoles search ahead of a rivalry weekend for both teams. FSU hosts Florida, and Georgia faces Georgia Tech, meaning any offcial annoucments would likely be made after the pair of games.

articles.headline: MLB Hot Stove tracker: Live updates on latest news, rumors, signings and trades in 2026 free agency
keyFacts: The heart of the MLB offseason is typically the first two weeks of December, but this isn't a typical offseason.
A lockout is set to take effect at the end of the day on Dec.
1, ending all transactions until the owners and players agree to a new collective bargaining agreement.
body: The heart of the MLB offseason is typically the first two weeks of December, but this isn't a typical offseason.

A lockout is set to take effect at the end of the day on Dec. 1, ending all transactions until the owners and players agree to a new collective bargaining agreement. As we saw five years ago, that will likely take some time.

2021 offers an indication of how offseason transactions could play out: there was a flurry of activity leading up to start of the lockout, but plenty of significant moves had to wait until after the lockout was lifted more than three months later.
If reports are any indication, though, No. 1 free agent Tarik Skubal has a strong chance to sign before the lockout begins, raising the level of intrigue around free agency.
The Sporting News is tracking the latest MLB rumors, signings and trades before the lockout begins. Follow along below with the latest news.
MORE: Tracking the latest Tarik Skubal rumors
MLB Hot Stove 2026: Latest news, rumors on signings and trades
Yankees sign reliever Brent Suter
- Date: Nov. 23
- Source: Jeff Passan

New York adds the 37-year-old Suter on a one-year deal worth $4 million as the Yankees aim to reshape their bullpen. Suter has been both a starter and reliever in his career, and he will start out the season in the Yankees' bullpen.
Teruaki Sato could sign before Thanksgiving
- Date: Nov. 23
- Source: Ken Rosenthal

The Japanese star needs to sign before the pending lockout next week, and it seems like he is on track to sign somewhere this week. The Phillies, Blue Jays, Yankees and Mets are all teams that have been linked to the slugger.
Mets add Paul Goldschmidt
- Date: Nov. 23
- Source: Jon Heyman

The veteran Goldshmidt isn't the star he used to be, but he can still defend at first base and hit lefties after serving as a platoon player with the Yankees. He will likely form a platoon with Jared Young at first base for the Mets next season.
Tarik Skubal agrees to deal with Mets

The Mets have agreed to a nine-year, $450 million deal with Skubal, Jon Heyman and Jeff Passan report. Skubal's free agency ends more than a week before the lockout as the Mets make him by far the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history in terms of both total value and average annual value.
Tigers add former Rookie of the Year Luis Gil
- Date: Nov. 22
- Source: Jeff Passan

The Tigers have agreed to a one-year, $2.3 million deal with non-tendered former Yankees starter Luis Gil. Gil was the AL Rookie of the Year in 2024 but has battled injuries and control issues over the last two seasons while also seeing his strikeout rate plummet.
Jarren Duran drawing interest from several teams
- Date: Nov. 22
- Source: Chris Cotillo, Sean McAdam

Red Sox OF Jarren Duran remains a trade candidate despite being tendered a contract and is drawing interest from the Padres, Phillies and Mariners, MassLive reports. The Cubs were previously reported as another suitor for Duran.
Ty France seeking 3-year deal
- Date: Nov. 21
- Source: Ken Rosenthal, Will Sammon

Fresh off a resurgent season with the Padres, free-agent Ty France is reportedly seeking a three-year deal. The Athletic reports France is looking for an average annual salary between Jake Bauers' $14.5 million and Jorge Polanco's $20 million from last winter.
Mets offered Skubal nine-year deal worth almost $400 million
- Date: Nov. 20
- Source: Jim Duquette

The Mets appear to be the most aggressive suitor for Skubal, with an initial offer that would allow Skubal to break multiple pitching contract records. Skubal also met with the Blue Jays, Dodgers and Padres thus far.
Cubs claim catcher Joey Bart off waivers
- Date: Nov. 20
- Source: Robert Murray

The former No. 2 overall pick heads to the Cubs after he played for multiple teams in 2026. He should be a depth catcher option and could ultimately replace Carson Kelly, who is a free agent this offseason.
Jonathan Loaisiga goes back to Yankees
- Date: Nov. 20
- Source: Jorge Castillo

It's a two-year deal for Loaisiga, with a club option for the 2029 season, as the reliever returns to New York after a year with the Diamondbacks. Loaisiga battled injuries in his first stint with the Yankees, but he was great for Arizona in 2026 as he had a bounce-back season, and now he cashes in.
Cubs 'extensively' scouting Teruaki Sato
- Date: Nov. 19
- Source: Patrick Mooney

The Cubs have "extensively" scouted Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, The Athletic's Patrick Mooney reports. Sato is currently posted for MLB teams and is the consensus top international free agent on the market.
Yankees involved in third base market
- Date: Nov. 19
- Source: Jon Morosi
The Yankees checked in on Maikel Garcia before he was traded, Jon Morosi reports, and are in the market for a third base upgrade.
Tarik Skubal still likely to sign before lockout
- Date: Nov. 19
- Source: Jon Heyman
Skubal has met with all four teams publicly reported as suitors and is "likely" to sign before the lockout takes effect at the end of Dec. 1, Jon Heyman reports.
Padres 'could be the favorites' for Seiya Suzuki

The Padres met with free-agent OF Seiya Suzuki on Monday and "could be the favorites" to sign him, according to Jeff Passan. Suzuki is one of this offseason's top available bats after a strong five seasons with the Cubs.
Twins ink Sonny Gray to 2-year deal
- Date: Nov. 18
- Source: Jon Heyman

Sonny Gray is returning to Minnesota for a second stint, as the Twins announced he has signed a two-year deal with the team. The deal is worth $55 million, according to Jon Heyman. Gray received down-ballot Cy Young votes in his lone season with the Red Sox, posting a 2.72 ERA across 29 starts.
Red Sox acquire Nick Fortes from Rays
- Date: Nov. 18
- Source: Jeff Passan

The Red Sox are acquiring catcher Nick Fortes from the Rays for 17-year-old pitching prospect Angel Roa. Fortes, 30, is a defense-first catcher who hit .258 with 6 home runs across 109 games in Tampa Bay last season.
Mariners acquire Maikel Garcia in 6-player deal
- Date: Nov. 18
- Source: Jeff Passan
The Mariners have acquired 3B Maikel Garcia, RP James McArthur and minor-league RP L.P. Langevin from the Royals, in exchange for SP Bryce Miller, SP Logan Evans and RP Jose Ferrer.

Garcia broke out as an All-Star in 2025 with an .800 OPS and Gold Glove defense. While he regressed offensively, Garcia offers a high floor with his excellent defense and is under team control through 2030.
Miller, under contract through 2029, gives the Royals an instant rotation option as Kansas City adds much-needed pitching across the board.
David Bednar, Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer
- Date: Nov. 17
- Source: Tyler Kepner

After four players took themselves off the market last winter by accepting qualifying offers, two did so on Tuesday: Yankees closer David Bednar and Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers will both return on the one-year, $23.15 million deal. Bednar notched 35 saves in a strong season as New York's closer in 2026, while Jeffers was limited to just 92 games but posted an .814 OPS and 2.8 WAR in that span.
White Sox sign SP Dustin May
- Date: Nov. 17
- Source: Robert Murray

The White Sox are signing May to a three-year contract worth "just north" of $50 million, per Murray. The right-hander won another World Series with the Brewers this past season, but has been up-and-down since a 2.63 ERA season with the Dodgers in 2023. May will bring some strikeout stuff to Chicago's rotation.
Brewers acquire reliever Ryan Walker from Giants
- Date: Nov. 15
- Source: Alex Pavlovic

The Giants have traded reliever Ryan Walker to the Brewers for minor-league pitchers Gavin Perry and Blake Holub. A standout with a 1.91 ERA in 2024, Walker regressed sharply in 2024 and fell out of the big-league bullpen with a 7.16 ERA in 2026; he's under team control through 2029.
Orioles, Diamondbacks discussing Ketel Marte swap
- Date: Nov. 14
- Source: Mike Rodriguez

The Orioles are reportedly interested in landing Marte from the Diamondbacks via trade. The three-time All-Star has twice finished inside the top-four in NL MVP voting. Marte, 33, posted a .748 OPS and 107 OPS+ in 562 at-bats last year.
Red Sox, Jake Bauers agree terms to four-year deal
- Date: Nov. 13
- Source: Jeff Passan

Boston locked up Bauers, the NLCS MVP, on a four-year, $58 million deal. Bauers, 31, enjoyed the best season of his big-league career in 2026, posting an .874 OPS and 140 OPS+ while slugging 26 home runs in 144 games.
Braves sign RP Evan Phillips
- Date: Nov. 12
- Source: Braves

The Braves add the reliever on a three-year, $35 million deal to help upgrade the bullpen and potentially replace Raisel Iglesias. Phillips broke out with the Dodgers since joining Los Angeles in 2021, totaling a 2.36 ERA in 232 games with the team.
Phillies expressing interest in Teruaki Sato, Seiya Suzuki, Randy Arozarena
- Date: Nov. 11
- Source: Matt Gelb

Philadelphia is looking to add an outfielder and has looked at three of the top bats in Sato, Suzuki and Arozarena; the Phillies are 'intrigued' by Sato, who has been posted to MLB teams after winning a triple-crown in Japan's Central League.
Yankees 'looking closely' at Alec Bohm
- Date: Nov. 11
- Source: Jon Heyman
The Yankees have been monitoring third baseman Alec Bohm on the free-agent market, with the potential to bring him in to hit primarily vs. left-handed pitchers.
Braves shut down ideas of trading Ronald Acuna Jr.
- Date: Nov. 11
- Source: Grant McAuley
After some rumors that the Braves could look into trading star outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr., Alex Anthopoulos shut them down, saying: "We are not trading Ronald Acuna Jr. Put it in bold."
Anthopoulos added that Atlanta has had " zero calls outgoing or incoming on trading Acuna."
Rangers 'intend to explore moving' SS Corey Seager
- Date: Nov. 11
- Source: Ken Rosenthal

Texas will explore the possibility of trading star shortstop Corey Seager at the GM meetings, though Rosenthal notes that it would be a challenge, as the infielder is owed $155 million over the next five seasons at 33 years old. Seager also has full no-trade protection as a player with 10 years of service time, including five consecutive with the same club.
Seager has also had recent injury issues, including elbow surgery in 2026, an appendectomy last year and a sports hernia the year before.
Nationals' Dylan Crews has emerged as trade target
- Date: Nov. 11
- Source: Spencer Nusbaum
Washington outfielder Dylan Crews has become a trade target, with "a number of teams" expressing interest, per Nusbaum. The former No. 2 pick posted a .663 OPS in 2026.
'At least six' teams to meet with Skubal, including Padres, Blue Jays
- Date: Nov. 11
- Source: Jon Heyman

According to Heyman, "at least six" teams have scheduled a meeting with star pitcher Tarik Skubal, including the Dodgers, Padres, Blue Jays and Mets. The process with Skubal is expected to move quickly after those meeting next week.
Tigers ink reliever Emilio Pagan on 1-year deal
- Date: Nov. 11
- Source: Jon Heyman
Detroit is signing former Reds reliever Emilio Pagan to a one-year, $11 million deal. He posted a 3.38 ERA and 25 saves in 28 chances in 2026.
Mets schedule meeting with Tarik Skubal
- Date: Nov. 10
- Source: Jon Heyman

The Mets have put a meeting with star pitcher Tarik Skubal on their calendar, per Heyman, as they consider an offer to the best player on the market. New York and the Dodgers have been considered the top players for Skubal, both with deep pockets to pull off a signing.

articles.headline: Iran vows to end U.S. naval blockade by "all available means"
keyFacts: Iran stated Monday that it will use all available means to counter a naval blockade on its ports, which it described as military aggression.
The U.S. Treasury Department issued new sanctions Monday against Iranian nationals and entities as part of an effort to disrupt global shadow banking networks.
Iranian judiciary authorities announced Monday that domestic courts awarded Iran $290 billion in damages against the United States.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:
- Iran said Monday it would use "all available means" to counter the of the country's ports, which a foreign ministry official described as "an act of military aggression" against the country.

- President Trump said in a social media post on Sunday that Iran had "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time" during the , but that the increasing attacks had "done no damage."

- A media outlet linked to Iran's Houthi allies said Monday that a Saudi attack on Yemen's port city of Hodeida killed four people and wounded 18, as fighting between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis continues to intensify.
Top Iranian diplomat calls land blockade of Iran "impossible"

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called a land blockade of Iran "impossible" in comments shared Monday, according to Iranian state media. He also said pushing back against U.S. sanctions "is the duty of the entire country and its people," state media reported.
"The best way to counter this pressure is to make those imposing sanctions lose hope of achieving their goals, so they know this tool is ineffective and will remain so," Araghchi said.
Qatar's prime minister returns to Washington for Rubio meeting
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, in Washington, D.C., on Monday.

It was the Qatari official's second visit to Washington in recent weeks, after meeting with President Trump earlier this month. At the time, Mr. Trump had said he didn't see a reason to escalate the Iran war after the midterm elections.
Qatar has been a key mediator in indirect talks between the U.S. and Iran to end the conflict, which have stalled.
U.S. issues dozens of new sanctions against Iran

The U.S. Treasury Department issued new sanctions against a group of Iranian nationals and entities, which it described as front companies and exchange houses, on Monday. A list of two dozen names posted to its website included nine Iranian individuals in addition to businesses based, mainly, in Tehran and Dubai.

The Treasury said in a news release that the sanctions came as part of "a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran's global shadow banking networks," which, according to the agency, allow billions to circulate internationally and "provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions."

"Iran's economy is underwater, and its leaders are panicking," said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in a statement. "Iran's shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime. Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake."
Coalition fighting Houthis carried out hundreds of strikes in last few hours, Yemen says

The military coalition fighting Houthi rebels in Yemen carried out 647 strikes in the last few hours, the Yemeni government said Monday. The attacks included drone, rocket, field artillery and airstrikes, a government spokesperson said in a social media statement.

According to the spokesperson, those strikes "targeted militia positions, gatherings, fortifications and movements" and resulted in the "neutralization" of 122 Houthi commanders and members. More than 50 vehicles and pieces of military equipment were destroyed or disabled, the statement said.

In a separate statement, also shared to social media, Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said the Saudi Air Force had carried out 67 airstrikes and missile attacks in the last 24 hours, and that dozens of civilians were killed or wounded.

Saree said the strikes killed and wounded dozens of civilians in targeted areas of Yemen's capital, Sana'a, as well as the governorates of Lahj, Taiz, Hodeidah, Saada and Hajjah. But the Yemeni government blamed the Houthis for a missile attack Monday in Taiz, where, its spokesperson said, two civilians were killed and seven others were injured in the village of Kahlan.
Houthis say death toll from Saudi attack has risen to 17

Yemen's Houthi rebels said the death toll from a Saudi attack on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida rose to 17 Monday. The Iran-backed fighters, who control a massive portion of Yemen, including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that supports Yemen's internationally recognized government.

Coalition airstrikes on telecommunication facilities killed 17 workers, wounded 11 more and caused the "total destruction" of administrative buildings, staff housing, a mosque and other infrastructure on the compound, the Houthis' telecommunications ministry said.
"This has led to the complete destruction of these facilities [and] the disruption of telecommunications and internet services," affecting tens of thousands of people, it said.

Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said in a social media post that another alleged Saudi coalition attack in the Lahj province, in Yemen's southwest, targeted buses and other vehicles. He said there were unspecified casualties.
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on either of the purported attacks. The coalition said Sunday that it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched at Saudi Arabia's western Red Sea coast.
CBS/AFP
U.S. discussing training Syrian armed forces, Reuters reports

The United States is discussing plans to train Syrian soldiers to conduct demining work, five people familiar with the matter told the Reuters news agency. The plan could see a small number of U.S. troops return to Syria as soon as next year if it is adopted.

The proposal is for a multinational training mission – made up of 15 countries including the U.K., France and Saudi Arabia – to focus on demining and ordnance disposal. It would be the first time since 2024 that U.S. troops had trained Syrian counterparts.
The U.S. State Department told Reuters that Washington welcomed having a partner in the Syrian capital, , who is committed to combating the terror group ISIS.
U.S. officials would need to do due diligence to screen all prospective Syrian recipients of the training before any funding is dedicated to the prospective project, two of the sources told Reuters.
Iranian singer convicted of "outraging public decency" lashed 74 times for performing without hijab

An Iranian singer has been lashed 74 times after being convicted of the crime of "outraging public decency" for performing without wearing the hijab head covering that is mandatory for women in the country.
Parastoo Ahmadi was lashed Monday over her 2024 live-streamed YouTube concert, according to her attorney, who was quoted by the reformist Iranian newspaper Emtemad.

The lawyer told Emtemad that Ahmadi and four members of her production team presented themselves to provincial authorities in the holy city of Qom Monday as required after their sentences were upheld in September by a local criminal court.
The criminal court in Qom upheld the convictions for "outraging public decency" citing "immoral" content posted online during Ahmadi's performance in December 2024, which went viral in Iran.
In addition to the 74 lashes, Parastoo and eight members of her team were also sentenced to a two-year ban on travel out of the country and a two-year ban on all "artistic activity."

Parastoo performed her concert in the Dayr-Gachin Caravanserai - an ancient site along the Silk Road route in Iran. It included themes of nationalism and popular uprising, and saw her openly flout both the Islamic Republic's dress code and a long-standing ban on women singing in public.
Netanyahu warns against downplaying "grave threats" facing Israel
Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's now-caretaker prime minister, said Monday that Israel is still facing "serious and grave threats," and he warned of the dangers of downplaying them.

He spoke shortly after his domestic political opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, said he saw no immediate threat posed by Iran that would warrant military action before a new Israeli government is formed to oust Netanyahu.

"Anyone who belittles or downplays these immediate, serious and grave threats surrounding us does so for political reasons," Netanyahu said at a briefing in Israel's parliament, in which he called for a unity government, as Eisenkot attempts to form a new ruling coalition.
CBS/AFP
Netanyahu foe trying to form new Israeli government says no "immediate threat" requiring action against Iran

Gadi Eisenkot, the Israeli politician trying to form a new government to oust current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the wake of national elections, has said he sees no "immediate threat" from Iran requiring military action.
Speaking at a meeting of his party, Yashar, Monday, he said: "I see no direct and immediate threat from Iran today that would require Israel to act before a new government is formed."
He added that "the gravest threat Iran poses" comes from its stockpile on enriched uranium: "That is where we need to focus."
Netanyahu has appeared keen to go on the offensive against Iran again. Sources familiar with the matter told CBS News last week that Israel and the U.S. were .

Eisenkot recently said Netanyahu should not make any big national security decisions in the transition period following Israel's election, in which Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority, and that the now-caretaker prime minister should avoid "dangerous steps that can wait for the swearing in of a new government."
Iran seeks $290 billion in damages against the U.S.

Iran is due $290 billion from the United States to cover damages inflicted both during, and long before the war launched jointly by the U.S. and Israel almost nine months ago, Iran's judiciary authorities say.
Iranian courts have demanded the U.S. pay the sum, a judiciary official said Monday.

"We have secured court rulings in domestic courts awarding $290 billion in damages against the Americans," said Hassan Abdolianpour, head of the judiciary's center for lawyers, according to state television.
He also said several lawsuits had been filed against Persian Gulf Arab nations for "allowing their territory to be used by America to launch attacks against Iran."
According to state TV, the damages cover U.S. actions going back decades.

On Monday, state broadcaster IRIB said several U.S.-linked commercial ships had been seized and that part of the compensation owed to Iran would be settled through the seizures, without giving further details.
CBS/AFP
Lebanon denounces Israeli military official's visit to school in south
Lebanese officials have denounced a visit by an Israeli military spokesperson to a school in an Israeli-occupied area of southern Lebanon.

As Lebanon marked its independence day on Sunday, the Israeli military's Arabic-language spokesperson Ella Waweya shared a video on social media showing her outside a school in Debl, a Christian village, and then standing in front of a classroom full of children.

The village is located inside a wide swath of southern Lebanon that Israel has occupied and declared a "security zone" after the latest war erupted with Hezbollah in March. The zone covers a strip of southern Lebanon along the border and stretches about six miles into Lebanese territory.

Debl is among a number of Christian-majority villages near the border where many residents have refused to leave despite Israeli military orders to evacuate. Cut off from the rest of Lebanon, they are largely dependent on humanitarian aid.

"During my last visit to south Lebanon, I was amazed by the beauty of the land and the villages which have paid a heavy price due to their exploitation ... by a terrorist organization," Waweya said, referring to the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group.
Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam denounced Israel for "dragging students into a military and propaganda display."
"An occupying power has no right to exploit our children to embellish the image of its occupation or impose its dominance over our people in the south," he added.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war in March with rocket fire at Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion. Lebanon says Israeli attacks since then have killed more than 4,300 people.
CBS/AFP
Iran says will use "all available means" to counter U.S. blockade
Iran said Monday it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz.
"We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in his weekly press briefing.
Soon after the war broke out, the Strait of Hormuz became the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies.
In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran.

"You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Baqaei. "Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the U.N. Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself."
Iran has said Hormuz could be open within two days but only if Washington agreed to its list of demands, which include the lifting of the blockade.
Houthi media say 4 dead in Saudi attack on key port city
Houthi media said Monday that a Saudi attack killed four people and wounded 18 in Yemen's key port city of Hodeida.
The Iran-backed fighters, who control large swathes of Yemen including Hodeida, are battling a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognized government.
The strike targeted a building belonging to Yemen's Public Telecommunications Corporation, the Houthis' Almasirah television channel wrote on X.
Riyadh didn't immediately comment on the report.
It came a day after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched toward the kingdom's western Red Sea coast.
That region is home to major oil installations that Houthi fighters have attacked in recent weeks, along with strikes on airports and military sites.
Yemen, which has been embroiled in more than a decade of civil war, was sucked into the U.S.-Iran conflict in July when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unraveled.
Since then, hostilities have left more than 1,600 people dead and more than 300,000 displaced in the country, the poorest on the Arabian Peninsula, according to the latest U.N. data.
Houthis say Saudi strike on Yemen capital wounds 6
Houthi rebels in Yemen reported an airstrike early Sunday in the capital, Sanaa.
A spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry, Anees al-Asbahi, said the strike hit a fuel station operated by the state-run oil company and wounded six workers.
The strike also damaged the company's building, al-Asbahi said.
The Red Sea port city of Mokha also came under fire on Sunday, Houthi-run television reported, as did the Haifan district in the southwestern province of Taiza.
The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia for the airstrikes but didn't report any casualties from them.
Trump says Iran launched more drones and missiles in past week "than at any time for over a year"

President Trump on Sunday acknowledged that Iran "has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but he added: "Don't worry, they've all been knocked down, and done no damage."
In a post on Truth Social, the president linked the midterm elections — in which in both chambers of Congress — to the escalation in the war with Iran.

"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran, which has killed 81,000 protestors as of today, will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," Mr. Trump said.
Higher fuel prices triggered by the war caused economic concerns for Americans, and top Republicans, have partly attributed GOP election defeats to the war with Iran.
Mr. Trump on Sunday said voters "didn't understand" what their votes meant and called the election "very 'strange.'"

"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won't let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," he said. "Too bad the Voters didn't understand this before they pulled the trigger, but the whole Election was very 'strange.'"
Athlete swims Strait of Hormuz to raise awareness of Iran war's toll on wildlife

British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum in the North Pole and Antarctica to draw attention to environmental causes. But battling freezing waters and extreme conditions hasn't prepared him for his latest challenge: swimming the while tankers are attacked and blown up nearby.
Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days this week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how the threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.

Wearing only swimming trunks, goggles and a cap bearing the U.N. logo, the athlete started from the Musandam Peninsula, on the southern tip of the strait, and ended by rounding the Cape of Hormuz, completing about 9.3 miles in total. Pugh is believed to be the first person to undertake a long-distance swim there since the war started.
The swimmer said that minutes after he entered the water on Monday, he heard two loud explosions that rocked the sea.
Iran holds talks with Qatari mediators
Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said on Saturday that a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and "held two hours of talks," without providing details.
Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran to end the war have stalled in recent months.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said, however, that ongoing talks in the region must be "given a chance" and that the ongoing U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz "must be lifted rationally."
"Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless," he said, quoted by state television.
"At the same time, we have always affirmed our readiness for dialogue, just as we are ready to defend ourselves."
Iran's conditions have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
CBS/AFP
Trump says he wants to make "permanent" deal with Iranian regime
President Trump said Saturday that he wants to make a "permanent" deal with Iran that will prevent the country from gaining a nuclear weapon in the future.

"What I'm doing is I'm going to make it so that if we have an incompetent president in four years or 15 years or 20 years, I'm going to make a deal that is going to be permanent," Mr. Trump told Fox News in a phone interview on Saturday. "I'm not going to let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon."

Mr. Trump said he's never "cared too much about the regime" leading Iran, and that he has "taken out two regimes already," though he declined to specify further. Former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed in the initial strikes on Iran that began the war in February 2026. His son Mojtaba Khamenei has held the title ever since.
Mr. Trump said Iranian officials have been "very, very difficult" to make a deal with.
"I mean, we make a deal and then they break the deal the next day," Mr. Trump said.

articles.headline: Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable "from the beginning to the end," Toby Fox says, but the RPG's final part has "only just started"
keyFacts: Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.
"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post.
"The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end.
body: Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)"

While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing."

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox said he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible."
And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way"
"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence."

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

articles.headline: Sources: 49ers releasing Aiyuk, ending WR's tumultuous tenure with team
keyFacts: The tumultuous relationship between the San Francisco 49ers and Brandon Aiyuk is ending as the team is releasing the wide receiver Monday, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
The move ends Aiyuk's tenure with the 49ers after about six and a half years.
Since his release is happening after the trade deadline, Aiyuk is subject to waivers.
body: The tumultuous relationship between the San Francisco 49ers and Brandon Aiyuk is ending as the team is releasing the wide receiver Monday, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The move ends Aiyuk's tenure with the 49ers after about six and a half years. Since his release is happening after the trade deadline, Aiyuk is subject to waivers. If he's unclaimed in the next 24 hours, he would become an unrestricted free agent who is free to sign anywhere.

Because the move is happening after June 1, the dead money remaining on his deal will be split into $12.35 million for 2026 and $19.29 million in 2027. The Niners will receive a cap credit of nearly $5 million in March and are also aiming to recoup additional bonus money from Aiyuk.

Aiyuk's release has been months in the making after Niners general manager John Lynch said the team would be moving on from him on Jan. 21. It only happened now because Aiyuk hired agent Drew Rosenhaus in late October, applied for reinstatement with the NFL and reported to the team on Nov. 6.
That day, Aiyuk, Rosenhaus and the Niners met for a little more than an hour with Aiyuk saying he is feeling "great" and "healthy."
"It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process," Aiyuk said then. "But I'm back to 100% and looking to get reinstated to the National Football League."
For their part, the Niners have sought repayment from Aiyuk for about $13 million in bonus money they had previously paid him.

The NFL officially reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9 after he reported for a physical. The league provided the Niners a two-week roster exemption to sort through any remaining business with Monday as the day that the exemption expired.

Because the exemption ended after the NFL trade deadline, the 49ers had just two options: release Aiyuk or keep him. Coach Kyle Shanahan and Lynch had remained adamant since January that Aiyuk was done as a Niner, which meant his release was always a matter of when, not if.

While Aiyuk's release always seemed inevitable, the Niners clung to hope that they could find a trade partner rather than releasing him. Along the way, Aiyuk repeatedly voiced his displeasure with how the Niners handled the situation as they continued to retain his contractual rights.

Despite a lack of interest and momentum toward a deal, San Francisco held on to Aiyuk through free agency, the draft and every other offseason benchmark. In early June, Aiyuk began to speak out publicly for the first time. In a pair of videos posted to Instagram, he called the 49ers "dumb" and "stupid" for paying him and suggested that the team was scared to release him because of how he might play for another team.

Just before that, on June 3, Aiyuk also dealt with the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office issuing a warrant for him on the misdemeanor charge of exhibition of speeding. That warrant is in reference to video Aiyuk posted to YouTube in December in which he appears to tape himself from the driver's seat going well over the posted 40 miles per hour speed limit on a road that runs past Levi's Stadium.

Through all that, rumors of Aiyuk's desire to play for the Washington Commanders and with quarterback Jayden Daniels (Aiyuk's close friend from Arizona State) persisted. He posted photos of himself in a Commanders hat, and Daniels and the Commanders were among the five accounts he followed on Instagram.

After an apparent rift with Daniels, Aiyuk and the Washington quarterback patched things up, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported on Nov. 18. That could potentially open the door for Aiyuk to land in Washington, though Rosenhaus has indicated multiple times that he has multiple interested teams for Aiyuk.

While Aiyuk is now free to sign anywhere, his departure ends a confounding partnership between team and player that began to deteriorate when the sides started negotiating a contract extension in 2024.

The Niners and Aiyuk went back and forth on a potential contract early in 2024 and, as other receivers around the league got paid, the price for Aiyuk continued to climb. Finally, the stalemate that had Aiyuk holding-in during that summer's training camp seemed to reach a conclusion when he signed a four-year, $120 million extension with $76 million in guarantees on Aug. 29, 2024.

At the time, the 49ers hoped the new deal would put any built-up issues with Aiyuk in the past but that vanished less than a month later. On Sept. 27, 2024, Aiyuk and Shanahan had an awkward exchange on the practice field when Aiyuk showed up wearing red shorts instead of the requisite black ones his teammates were wearing.

From there, the sides never seemed to get on the same page again with Aiyuk struggling early in the season as he averaged 58.5 receiving yards per game with no touchdowns in the first six games. He tore the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee against the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 20, 2024, ending his season. It would be the last game he'd play as a Niner.

The 49ers also hoped to trade Aiyuk last offseason, sources told ESPN, but the injury made getting a good return in a potential deal unrealistic and that never gained traction. Aiyuk's $24.935 million roster bonus for 2026 became guaranteed on April 1, 2025, effectively ensuring he'd be with the Niners for the 2025 season.

Hopes that Aiyuk would return and contribute existed for chunks of the offseason, but when he didn't show up for multiple in-house rehab sessions, the Niners voided the roughly $27 million in guarantees Aiyuk's contract held for 2026 in July of last year.

On Nov. 22, 2025, Shanahan said that in more than two decades coaching he'd never had a situation when a player's contract was voided. Around that time, Aiyuk stopped reporting to the Niners facility altogether and cut off communication with the franchise's leadership.

"It's something I've never seen in 22 years of coaching," Shanahan said at the time. "It's unfortunate and it's confusing because it's confusing for all of us, but it eventually becomes it is what it is."

On Dec. 13, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left team list, a designation that ended Aiyuk's season and any chance he would play for the team again. He did not report for or participate in any of the team's offseason program or training camp, either.

At his end-of-season news conference, Lynch said moving on from Aiyuk would allow for more salary cap flexibility, though most of that will come in future years. Lynch added he "wish I knew" why Aiyuk stopped communicating with the team.
Before his knee injury, Aiyuk had emerged as one of the league's most productive wideouts. He had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on his way to second-team All-Pro honors in 2023.
Originally a first-round pick (No. 25) in the 2020 NFL draft, Aiyuk had 294 receptions for 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns in 69 regular-season games for the 49ers.

Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now

Claude Ship is now available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and works with repositories on GitHub.

I’m going to let you in on a secret: despite having access to some amazing gaming laptops, I rarely use them when I want to play a game.

At heart, I’m a desktop PC guy. I love building my own PC, and the customization options and upgradability make them my favorite way to play. Not to mention, desktop components can be much more powerful than mobile variants.

Gaming laptops always felt to me like a cut-down compromise, as you sacrificed all of that for a device that’s more portable, but because you’ll still need to play your games with the laptop plugged in (graphically demanding games will deplete your battery quickly), and most likely on a desk so you can use a gaming mouse.

Of course, gaming laptops do have their uses, and I can completely understand why someone would rather have one of those instead of a gaming desktop PC. They’re more convenient and easier to set up, can be taken with you when travelling, and don’t occupy as much space as a traditional gaming rig.

But as a desktop-first gamer, I’ve been increasingly drawn to handheld gaming PCs, starting with the Steam Deck and my beloved ROG Ally X, and I’ve been increasingly enamored with the latest generation of handhelds such as the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ and the Acer Predator Atlas 8, which I’m currently reviewing.

“Matt! You hypocrite!” I can sense some of you thinking. Those gaming handhelds suffer from all the compromises I just reeled off when attacking gaming laptops. You can’t upgrade them, they aren’t as customizable, and less powerful than desktops. But with gaming handhelds, those compromises simply don’t matter as much to me, and it’s for one very simple reason: the form factor.

With traditional gaming laptops, I still play on them as I would with a desktop PC, which doesn’t just highlight the shortcomings of a gaming laptop compared to my powerful gaming PC, but it also limits where and when I play on it.
Handheld gaming PCs, however, have completely different designs. As their name suggests, they are designed to be held in your hand, with built-in gamepad controls and relatively small touchscreens.

This instantly makes them more convenient for playing while travelling, as they are smaller and lighter than gaming laptops, and you don’t need a surface to place them on. The smaller screens also mean some of the graphical settings you need to turn down aren’t as noticeable.

Handhelds also force me to play different games due to the built-in controller. For genres where mouse and keyboard are best, such as management sims, real-time strategy, and first-person shooters, I leave that to my gaming PC.

On a handheld, I stick to indie games, platformers, third-person RPGs, arcade games, and other genres I’ve often neglected. It lets me do some deep dives into my Steam, GOG, and Epic Games Store backlogs and mix up my playstyle.
Of course, if you have no interest in those latter genres, a gaming laptop will be a better buy.
What about performance?

If you care about pure performance, as many PC gamers understandably do, then a gaming laptop with a dedicated graphics card is going to easily outperform a handheld, as its smaller size forces it to rely on less powerful integrated graphics.

However, mobile components have come a long way these past few years, and recent handhelds powered by the Intel Arc G3 Extreme are seriously impressive, allowing handhelds to run graphically intensive games such as Cyberpunk 2077 at 60fps and over, with a bit of tweaking.

While you do need to lower some settings to keep frame rates playable, as I mentioned earlier, the smaller screens of handhelds are more forgiving if you drop certain settings and even resolutions to help smooth out performance.

Sticking to older games, or less graphically demanding indie titles, is another good way to get the most out of a gaming handheld. For example, I’m trying to take my mind off the fact that it seems everyone else in the world is enjoying GTA 6 by playing GTA Vice City The Definitive Edition on the Acer Predator Atlas 8, and while I know deep down it’s not going to compete with the latest game from Rockstar, it’s still a bit of a thrill playing an open-world game I first explored on the PlayStation 2 on a device I’m holding in my hands.
What’s the cost?

This is where things get a bit tricky, and why Black Friday deals could really help. Back when the Steam Deck, arguably the first of this modern breed of handheld gaming PCs, launched in 2022 beginning at $399 / £349 (it launched later in Australia), it was a no-brainer for a lot of people.

You simply couldn’t get a gaming laptop for around that price (unless it was very old or underpowered), and even to people with a bit more cash to spend, I was suggesting they consider the Steam Deck over slightly more expensive gaming laptops.

The current situation in 2026 is very different, sadly. The global memory shortage, sometimes called the ‘RAMpocalypse’ has seen prices for all kinds of devices, including both handhelds and gaming laptops, rise steeply.

Back in May, Valve raised the price of its Steam Deck OLED handheld by 50%, so it now starts at $789 / £649 / AU$1,199. Considering that apart from a nicer screen and more storage space to start, this handheld is still running on the same hardware as four years ago, I simply can’t recommend it anymore.
More recent handhelds have launched at wince-inducingly high prices, such as the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, which began at $1,799.99 / £1,399.99 / AU$2,849.
When handhelds start costing as much as upper-midrange gaming laptops, they become a lot harder to justify. Unfortunately for us gamers, gaming laptops have also gone up in price as well.

Still, for around that same price, you could get something like the Acer Nitro V16 from Amazon, which comes with 32GB RAM, an AMD Ryzen 7 processor, and an Nvidia RTX 5070 GPU. This will absolutely destroy the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ when it comes to performance, so it then boils down to the form factor, as you’re paying a premium for the smaller, more portable build of the Claw 8 EX AI+ compared to the Nitro V16, which, as a 16-inch gaming laptop that weighs 4.85lbs (2.2kg), won’t be the most comfortable device to lug around with you.

This is why this year’s Black Friday sales (many of which have already started) could be a real game changer. Not only am I expecting plenty of tempting gaming laptop Black Friday deals, but there should be some great handheld gaming PC deals as well.

Just this weekend, the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ dropped by £300 in the UK for a limited time, and while that deal has ended, I expect similar deals to crop up this week in the run-up to Black Friday itself on Friday 27. That £300 discount suddenly made the Claw 8 much better value, especially when compared to gaming laptops around that same price.
That’s given me hope that Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals this year could make PC gaming great again, by giving us at least a small break in the price rise misery.

body: President Donald Trump warned Monday that he would hold Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D-IA) responsible for any deaths or destruction resulting from a dangerous stockpile of explosives if he refuses to approve the Army’s plan to detonate the materials.

Trump threw his support behind the military’s proposed controlled explosion at a World War II-era ammunition plant in Iowa , arguing that deteriorating explosives pose a growing threat to nearby communities and that detonating them now is safer than waiting for a potentially catastrophic accident.

But the president said the operation would not move forward until the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals clears the way and Sand agrees to the plan. If either refuses, Trump said, the military would have no choice but to leave the hazardous materials in place.

“The Experts, in particular the United States Military, feel that this approach will be a far safer one than allowing the situation to fester, not knowing when they will detonate by themselves,” Trump wrote in a lengthy Truth Social post . “This operation would, in other words, be a controlled one rather than a large, spontaneous explosion. The weather, right now, is optimal for this planned response to take place. I feel the proper course is to get rid of this longterm problem but, at the same time, have ordered the Military not to do so until such time as the Eighth Circuit agrees that we can go forward, and am further making this decision fully subject to the incoming Governor Elect, Rob Sand, agreeing to the operation.”

Regarding Sand, Trump continued, “If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation.”
Sand will not take office until Jan. 12, 2027. He is succeeding Gov. Kim Reynolds (R-IA).

The Army announced Sunday that it planned to detonate roughly 5 tons of degraded lead azide on Wednesday. But the planned blast has faced legal and environmental opposition, with critics warning that detonating the material in the open could send toxic lead dust into the air and contaminate nearby homes and farmland.

The operation was initially scheduled for Friday but was delayed as the appeals court considered a lawsuit challenging the Army’s plans. A judge issued a temporary stay on the Environmental Protection Agency permit authorizing the blast. The Army subsequently pushed the planned detonation to Monday, then Tuesday, and ultimately Wednesday to accommodate weather conditions and allow additional safety measures to be put in place.

The EPA issued a permit effective Nov. 13 authorizing a controlled detonation, citing the need to address the explosive hazard and mitigate an imminent threat to the surrounding community and environment.

The Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club sued to block the operation, arguing that the Army failed to inform the public adequately about the planned explosion and its potential consequences. But the Pentagon has argued that the operation can proceed on an emergency basis under EPA regulations, without requiring a permit.

Sand, who defeated Trump-backed Republican candidate Zach Lahn in the midterm elections, has called for greater transparency and accountability from federal officials, while emphasizing that protecting Iowans must remain the priority.

“Because of the decisions that have already been made over the course of months, if not years, no good options exist and the situation is more dangerous and unpredictable than it ever should have been,” Sand wrote Sunday.
Iowa lead explosion: How did we get here?
He also questioned why a contract to remove the explosive hazard, signed in the spring, was canceled and why officials are now rushing to carry out a detonation in late November.

The dispute carries particular political significance in Iowa, where environmental concerns have become a major issue. Concerns about agricultural chemicals and contaminants in drinking water also featured prominently in the midterm elections, helping shape the political environment in which Sand and other Democrats secured victories.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang’s return proves Trump and the tech right still call the shots
keyFacts: A television broadcasts Nvidia news on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) on November 23, 2026.
| Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty For a brief moment after the 2026 midterms, it had seemed that President Donald Trump was a true lame duck already.
First came Democrats’ blue tsunami, a popular rejection of his record by voters that threatens to constrain much of his agenda.
body: A television broadcasts Nvidia news on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) on November 23, 2026. | Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty
For a brief moment after the 2026 midterms, it had seemed that President Donald Trump was a true lame duck already.

First came Democrats’ blue tsunami, a popular rejection of his record by voters that threatens to constrain much of his agenda. Then there was the ouster of Jensen Huang , a celebrity CEO who had been deeply influential on the Trump administration’s AI and chip policy, to bipartisan chagrin , and was arguably the single most important private individual in the broader economy .

Huang’s downfall came after allegations that he had affairs with two employees as well as a tech executive who some US officials thought was a Chinese spy . And it seemed to signify that the era in which Trump and the tech right — a group of wealthy venture capitalists and CEOs who backed Trump, such as Elon Musk and David Sacks — ran the country was over.
Not so fast. Just 11 days after Huang resigned, Nvidia made the shocking announcement Monday that it was putting him back in the CEO job.

And the company did so after a very public campaign from leading tech right figures and Trump . The president reportedly called into Nvidia’s board meeting as the company weighed Huang’s return, and in a CNBC interview Monday, Trump referred to the outcome as a “deal” that he’d made. “I spoke to them. Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them,” he said .

In their own announcement, Nvidia indicated that the White House assured them Huang was not a security liability, even as the company said it would continue its own internal investigation. Trump quickly confirmed that these assurances came from the very top.

“The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security,” Trump posted on Truth Social . “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
“On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure,” Trump added.
Meanwhile, tech investors aligned with Trump popped the champagne as soon as the news broke.
“The mistake,” Musk tweeted , “has been corrected.”

It’s an astonishing sequence of events — and a flex of power by the president and the tech right. Trump personally intervened to ensure one of the biggest companies in the world would once again be led by an executive embroiled in a personal misconduct and national security scandal.

In the CNBC interview Monday, Trump dismissed the national security concerns in a rather odd way. He said that, in fact, ousting Huang as CEO would be worse for national security, because Xi Jinping might lure him over to lead a Chinese company, and Huang may have done it out of anger because he has “a little blood in him.”

At least part of Trump’s motivation may have been the headwinds facing the tech-and-AI-powered stock market in recent weeks, including a brutal day of declines on Friday that led many to question whether a bubble had finally popped.

If Trump’s goal was to juice the markets, it worked — at least for now. Indeed, in the first minute after trading opened, the value of Nvidia increased about 33 percent . That’s $1 trillion in value that, in the minds of investors, would not have existed if not for Huang’s return.

But Huang’s restoration amidst scandal also seemed to epitomize the philosophy Trump had once infamously expressed, in a very different context : “I could stand in the middle of Fifth Avenue and shoot somebody, and I wouldn’t lose any voters, okay?” It’s a massive test of whether Trump’s ability to survive scandal after scandal on the basis of charisma and political hardball is transferable to someone else, even a CEO who has drawn his company into an international crisis with his personal behavior.

All this seemed exemplified in a bizarre Truth Social post from Trump Monday morning : an AI-generated image re-creating the famed photo of Trump rising bloodied after his 2024 assassination attempt — only with Huang in Trump’s place, a flag with Nvidia’s logo flying, and Huang raising a red bra.
From our President and Nvidia’s 12th board member (yes, this is a real post) pic.twitter.com/PgXo9nMlaN
— Rohan Goswami (@rogoswami) November 23, 2026
But can it last?

Huang’s return is an incredible display of resilience — for now. He still has his many enemies in Washington, among both political parties, some of whom are already warning him and his backers not to get too comfortable.

Those problems start with the incoming Democrats in Congress, who will soon have subpoena power in both the House of Representatives and the Senate — and who will now be more motivated than ever to investigate this topic. Even before they take over, Huang is set to testify before the Senate, as is Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick , the Cabinet official most closely associated with the pro-Huang bloc and whose dovish approach to Chinese chips has come under bipartisan fire.

“Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain,” Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY) — in the midst of a contested bid to regain his old post as majority leader — posted on X .

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), in line to chair the Senate Banking Committee, posted that the decision to reinstate Huang was “reckless,” adding : “The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what ‘input’ was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.”

But this issue is not confined to Trump’s partisan opponents either. Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE), freshly reelected to a new six-year term, warned on Monday that the decision “doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns” and strongly criticized Huang’s behavior. “I’ve served on a public company board,” he wrote on X. “His behavior does not support reinstatement.”

Sen. John Curtis (R-UT), meanwhile, wanted to know more about the Trump administration’s involvement. “Who in our government weighed in?” Curtis posted . “What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?”

Sen. Kevin Cramer (R-ND) went even further, asserting that Huang “may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws,” and saying his rehiring caused a serious “national security risk.”

Indeed, there’s significant Republican antipathy toward Huang as well among “China hawks,” who have long viewed Huang’s enthusiasm for selling Nvidia’s chips abroad — including, in the case of certain chips, to China — as harmful to American national security and the US’s place at the front of the AI race.

They were sharply critical of Huang well before news broke of Huang’s affair with a purported spy. “China hawks are patient and have long memories,” former congressional defense policy aide Eric Sayers wrote in criticism of Huang last year, and repeated as the Huang scandals were emerging.

These hawks include longtime members of Washington’s national security establishment and many GOP senators and members of Congress, as well as some of Trump’s own top officials — like Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Days after Huang’s ouster, the hawks seemed newly empowered, as the Trump administration issued a rule to crack down on chip sales abroad and Chinese remote access to American AI technology — a policy Huang’s allies in the administration had previously resisted.

Bessent in particular had seemed triumphant after Huang’s downfall. Last week, he said on Fox Business that the company needed “a dramatic shake-up” and that, “as the board conducts a search for a new leader, they need to go outside the company.”
But after Trump started to champion Huang’s return, Bessent changed his tune , attempting to argue that Huang’s restoration would meet his standard because “Jensen is on the outside now.”

Huang’s enemies will be watching him — and Nvidia and the White House — like a hawk for any sign of deference to China or for new information that might put Huang’s leadership role back into question.

And with corruption emerging as a major political liability for both Trump and his party, any suspected signs of favor-trading or profiteering — Huang’s $25 million donation to the presidential ballroom has already drawn attention, as well as Trump’s multimillion-dollar Nvidia trades — will face intense scrutiny as well, especially from newly empowered Democratic legislators.
“The President is selling out our national security to keep the stock market high and probably for some fucking donation to his ballroom,” Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) posted on X on Monday
For now, though, these critics’ attacks and concerns have all been swept away. Trump remains the most powerful man in the country — and often, he can still get his way.
Update, November 23, 2026, 2:55 pm ET: This post was originally published midday Monday. It has been updated to include more statements from senators.

body: Brandon Aiyuk's time in San Francisco has apparently come to an end. The 49ers have released Aiyuk, who will now look to continue his career with a new team, according to a report from ESPN.

The 49ers were given a two-week roster exemption when the NFL reinstated Aiyuk on Nov. 9. With that exemption ending on Nov. 23, the 49ers elected to move on from Aiyuk, who hasn't played an NFL game since tearing his ACL and MCL during the 2024 season. Aiyuk had signed a four-year, $120 deal with the 49ers that offseason following a tumultuous negotiation. That contract, as currently structured, still has two years remaining, with a 2027 cap hit of $40.5 million according to Over the Cap, meaning Aiyuk will likely need to clear waivers before any team formally signs him.

Aiyuk started the 2025 season on the PUP list. That November, it was reported that the 49ers voided the guaranteed money in his contract for 2026 due to lack of participation. In December, the 49ers placed him on their reserve/left squad list.

This summer, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/did not report list (meaning the 49ers were not obligated to pay him and he did not count against their roster) after he did not report to training camp. Aiyuk had since applied for reinstatement with the NFL and was granted it earlier this month.

Before 2024, Aiyuk enjoyed a productive career with the 49ers, who selected him with the 25th overall pick in the 2020 draft. In 2022, he eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards for the first time and caught a career-high eight touchdowns. The following season, he recorded a career-high 1,342 receiving yards while helping the 49ers reach the Super Bowl.

While his recent actions in San Francisco might scare some teams off, Aiyuk will likely draw interest from teams that need help at receiver. Aiyuk has long been linked to the Commanders; he and Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels were teammates at Arizona State. The Steelers are another team that could potentially be a landing spot for Aiyuk.
Despite not having Aiyuk, the 49ers are 9-1 and would be the No. 1 seed in the NFL if the playoffs started today.

body: In my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.

I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.
Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a new patch that went out today.

"Fixed an issue that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.

You don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. GTA 6 has realistically detailed radio towers that left a TikTok guy who's worked on them in real life gobsmacked. It would've been bizarre if Rockstar neglected to put that kind of effort into a system normies like me would notice within a few hours.

The sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes, I'm excited to see how much the weather affects the mood. I'll just have to remember to be a little more discerning when chasing down one of GTA 6's cars to make sure I don't absolutely ruin the interior from a surprise storm.

articles.headline: NVIDIA's Jensen Huang will testify publicly before senators on December 3
keyFacts: NVIDIA's Jensen Huang will testify publicly before senators on December 3 It’s going to be a busy few days in Washington DC for the freshly reinstated CEO.
A week after reclaiming his job as NVIDIA CEO, Jensen Huang will be heading to Washington DC for two hearings in front of lawmakers.
It had already been confirmed that Huang will face a trio of House committees on December 1.
body: NVIDIA's Jensen Huang will testify publicly before senators on December 3
It’s going to be a busy few days in Washington DC for the freshly reinstated CEO.

A week after reclaiming his job as NVIDIA CEO, Jensen Huang will be heading to Washington DC for two hearings in front of lawmakers. It had already been confirmed that Huang will face a trio of House committees on December 1. While that testimony is slated to take place behind closed doors, the Senate Banking Committee will instead grill Huang in a public hearing on December 3. Get the popcorn ready for that one.

In a statement to Bloomberg, committee chair Sen. Tim Scott said the hearing will focus on oversight of US export controls. The committee initially asked Huang to testify after he admitted to an affair. Reports had linked him with an executive at a company to which NVIDIA is said to have sold over $4 billion worth of chips and other equipment. US officials suspect that executive, Alice Huang, of being a Chinese spy.

Since 2024, the US Commerce and Justice departments have been investigating Megaspeed, the Singaporean cloud computing company she worked for between 2023 and 2025. Alice Huang is also reportedly under investigation over alleged links to Chinese AI companies that may have violated US export rules by smuggling in chips from the likes of NVIDIA and Super Micro Computer.

NVIDIA opened its own investigation following reports of the affair. The New York Times later reported he had another affair, this time with an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. He resigned from the company the next day, November 12.

On Monday, NVIDIA's board said it had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO and president, effective immediately, after receiving assurances from high-level US officials that bringing him back in wouldn't pose a threat to national security. President Donald Trump (whose investment accounts have traded tens of millions of dollars of NVIDIA stock during his second term) said he convinced the board to reappoint Huang.

NVIDIA last week established an export control compliance committee and on Monday said it was looking to appoint someone in a new position of Chief Compliance Officer. Both the company's investigation and the Banking Committee's probe are ongoing.

"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with US export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat member of the committee, said in a statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement. Jensen Huang's return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk."

Along with colleagues from both sides of the aisle, Warren is pushing forward legislation that would more tightly restrict NVIDIA exports. The AI Overwatch Act would codify Trump's limitations on chip exports to "foreign adversaries" into law. The Chip Security Act would force NVIDIA and other companies to monitor the locations of chips they send abroad. The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act would strengthen semiconductor export controls for the US and its allies. According to Bloomberg, final talks are underway to roll these bills into an annual defense package that lawmakers usually pass in December.

Rep. Shomari Figures, D-Ala., urged Democrats to not make oversight investigations the center of their party’s agenda over the next two years with a majority in both the House and the Senate. He said the upcoming years should be focused on "leveraging this majority" to bring results to Americans.

"I think there will obviously be some degree of oversight into what happened with DOGE, and I think rightfully so," Figures said. "But I don't believe that sort of oversight can become the North Star of what the party is all about over the next two years."

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who was just elected by his party to serve as speaker of the House, also recently left the door open to potential investigations into Musk when asked by Fox News Digital about the conversations surrounding oversight. He deferred leaving investigation decisions up to Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif. — the party’s expected leaders of oversight work.
The Republicans whom Fox News Digital spoke with were not totally convinced that Musk’s recent comments meant he was backing out of supporting Republicans.
"I think Musk is about fiscal responsibility," Rep. Glenn Grothman, R-Wis., said. "And the Republican Party, while it lets you down some of the time, is still the party of fiscal responsibility."

"It's totally in his hands, whether he supports [Republicans] or not," Rep. Kat Cammack, R-Fla., said. "But I don't think that there's any question that this Congress fell short, specifically the Senate, and people have a right to be angry. Hell, I'm angry."
Congressional oversight into Musk could come as soon as January, when Democrats officially take control of Congress and leadership of the House Oversight Committee.

articles.headline: Are Man Utd genuinely in a relegation battle?
keyFacts: Are Manchester United in a relegation battle?

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher assess their survival chances After Manchester United's 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino's side officially have the worst defence in Europe and have endured their worst start to a season in over half a century - so are they going down?
Monday 23 November 2026 19:56, UK What started as a blip has become a problem far more systemic for Man Utd.
body: Are Manchester United in a relegation battle? Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher assess their survival chances

After Manchester United's 4-0 thrashing at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino's side officially have the worst defence in Europe and have endured their worst start to a season in over half a century - so are they going down?
Monday 23 November 2026 19:56, UK
What started as a blip has become a problem far more systemic for Man Utd.

"If the name wasn't Man Utd and you're watching their performances, you'd say they are a team in a relegation fight. They're conceding lots of goals, a comedy of errors, red cards - they've won one game all season," said Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher.
Only Ipswich beaten in 11 attempts, the worst defence in Europe - and a 4-0 hammering at Liverpool on Sunday to wipe the gloss off Mauricio Pochettino's arrival within 12 first-half minutes.
Carragher added: "This Manchester United back four can't cope with pace. They're a million miles off it in terms of coming up against what they are in the Premier League."
The unthinkable is beginning to become thinkable. Are United in an actual relegation battle now?
