"They're in a relegation fight right now because of where they are in the table," said Carragher after a fifth defeat of the season left them with their lowest points tally at this stage of a season since 1972. "You can't say anything else when you look at their record this season.

"We don't believe it will happen over a 38-game season, but they haven't had the most difficult of starts. They've played a lot of promoted teams; they haven't played the best team in the league, Arsenal, yet.
"I don't think they'll go down, but this idea that they haven't got a scrap on their hands, they have."

It seems unfathomable. But should it? The numbers don't give Pochettino any grounds for optimism. Only 26 teams - barely one a season - have picked up eight points or fewer from their opening 11 games in the history of the Premier League and only 13 of those, exactly half, avoided the drop.

Of course, most of those were not clubs anywhere near the size and stature of Manchester United. But even the Opta supercomputer, which provides far more contextualised feedback, is losing faith and gives them a 24 per cent chance of going down - though it does still back them to stumble to safety and finish 16th.

"You wonder how low it can get," said Gary Neville after Sunday's defeat. "It's embarrassing. I don't believe they're in a relegation fight, they'll get out of this, but this is the worst Man Utd have been in 53 years. The worst defensive team in Europe, second-bottom in the league, they've never started this badly.
"Mauricio Pochettino's options aren't great."

That may be putting it lightly. As well as the worst defence in Europe's top-five leagues across all competitions, United also have the third-worst performing attack in the Premier League, falling below their xG tally by 4.2 goals already.
In an immediately infamous tweet in 2014, then-boss David Moyes was quoted as saying United "must improve in a number of areas, including passing, creating chances and defending".

Pochettino is unlikely to admit it publicly, but behind closed doors must have similarly widespread concerns even at this early stage. United have not found themselves in the bottom two after 11 games in 40 years.
Sir Alex Ferguson was brought in as their eventual saviour that winter, but turning the tide on this United side is a significantly bigger ask.

Are there personnel at his disposal who could improve matters? Potentially. Neville did pinpoint a back four of Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Diego Dalot who could at least get United out of their defensive slump.
"It's a poor back four, but it's their best back four. It could compete," he added. "But the one that started today and finished against Villa a few weeks ago, that'll get you relegated."

There is good news and bad news. Neville's quartet are unbeaten in every game they have started together since the start of 2023/24 - and can boast a 70-per-cent win ratio. Unfortunately for Pochettino, that only amounts to 10 games across more than three seasons, owing largely to availability.

But that still does not solve the problem of their limp attack. Of the 22 players to have attempted a shot for the club this season, 19 have under-performed their xG, and the three who have not, Benjamin Sesko, Joshua Zirkzee and Youri Tielemans, have scored only a solitary goal apiece.

There remain huge question marks over the Man Utd dressing room, its commitment and a lack of leadership which permeated into the public sphere in the final weeks of Michael Carrick's reign. Though Pochettino's players have shown they can perform when they want to. Carrick himself knows that better than anyone.

But his successor barely has time to address it over the next few weeks, with only one free midweek between now and the end of 2026 - and even then he has a trip to the Emirates, live on Sky Sports on December 20, to face at the end of his first uninterrupted week on the training pitch.

By that point United will be almost half-way through the Premier League season - and alarm bells will be ringing even louder if they still find themselves in the quagmire, especially with rock bottom Crystal Palace and promoted Coventry to come before then.
But might even that prove problematic for Pochettino?

"If you look at the strength of the Premier League this season, in terms of what we would call the teams you'd expect to be mid-table or near the bottom - it's probably as strong as it's ever been," said Carragher.
"There's no poor teams. There's not many great teams, but there's no poor teams.
"And that's a problem for Man Utd."

articles.headline: Airline glitches and storms could make Thanksgiving travel messy
keyFacts: Traveling for the Thanksgiving holiday is shaping up to be a bit chaotic, following a cascade of glitches that have upended airlines the past weeks, the threat of storms on both coasts and soaring airfares.

body: Traveling for the Thanksgiving holiday is shaping up to be a bit chaotic, following a cascade of glitches that have upended airlines the past weeks, the threat of storms on both coasts and soaring airfares.
No wonder Americans are feeling jittery going into the busiest travel week of the year.
On top of all that, there's concern that a big storm brewing along the East Coast could ground the big balloons in the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.
Flight delays and cancellations
The biggest unknown for travelers is whether airlines will be upended again by new system failures.

First there was the Federal Aviation Administration's network malfunction setting off the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years. Then last week, both United Airlines and Delta Air Lines saw their own outages, leading to hundreds of flight delays.

"You do your best to be patient, but it's also helpful to have some context of what's going on, because our lives are literally in your hands," said Chianti Blackmon, a college administrator who was at the Atlanta airport on Monday.
Delta said that its operations were stable Monday, a day after over 1,000 of its flights were delayed after an automated system that calculates aircraft weight malfunctioned.
"Delta teams are focused on keeping the operation moving safely and caring for our customers," the airline said.
Roundtrip domestic tickets for Thanksgiving are up more than one-third from the same time last year, according to estimates made in late October by the travel-booking company Hopper.
Wicked weather on both coasts

Holiday travelers can expect a rainy week on the East and West coasts and dry conditions in the nation's mid-section, said Joe Wegman, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service's Weather Prediction Center.

Many eyes are on an East Coast system. Heavy rain and high winds are expected to start Wednesday night along the coast of the Carolinas, hit the New York City area on Thanksgiving Day and reach Maine by Friday, he said.

The windy forecast was causing concerns about whether the big balloons will be able to fly during the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York. City law prohibits Macy's from flying full-size balloons if sustained winds exceed 23 mph (37 kph) or wind gusts are over 35 mph (56 kph).
The weather service said it expected the rain in New York to hold off until after the parade ends, but winds could be an issue.

"This is poor timing with the storm coming up on Thanksgiving Day," Wegman said. "Perhaps better timing that it's happening on Thanksgiving Day rather on any of the travel days before and after."

Rainy and windy weather also was expected on the West Coast. Moderate to major coastal flooding was forecast from Washington state to Southern California because of possible record-breaking king tides.
Thanksgiving snow for some in the US

Rain was forecast for the Pacific Northwest on Monday, and expected to spread to northern and central California by Wednesday morning with snow possible in higher elevations, the weather service said.
Snow was forecast Monday for parts of the Rockies, northern Michigan, western New York state and northwestern Pennsylvania.

"Across the U.S., certainly check with your local airports and airlines for any possible delays," Wegman said. "I think weather won't be a significant factor except on Thanksgiving Day itself, and if there are any lingering impacts into Friday morning perhaps from delays that happen on Thanksgiving Day."
Seewer reported from Toledo, Ohio. Associated Press reporters Emilie Megnien in Atlanta; Kathy McCormack in Concord, New Hampshire; and Dave Collins in Hartford, Connecticut, contributed.

body: Jensen Huang is back. The Nvidia CEO and founder, who was ousted from his company a little over a week ago after revelations of two extramarital affairs (including, critically, a dalliance with a suspected Chinese spy), has apparently been deemed too big to fail.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and subsequently grew the chipmaker into one of the most powerful companies in the world, has now been reinstated by the company’s board. The move was one that President Trump lobbied for. On Monday, after Huang’s return was announced, the President posted an AI-generated meme of the CEO holding a woman’s bra, an image that recalled the famous photo from Trump’s own assassination attempt.

Just how and why all of this has happened is a question that everybody is still scrambling to figure out. Because Nvidia is an economically important company, it is also a politically important one. Yet there’s a lot of disagreement over just how important Huang, himself, is — and whether his importance outweighs the alleged dangers of Chinese espionage to which his affair with Alice Huang may have exposed the company.

Even if Huang is back for now, the Nvidia founder may face an uphill battle given the changing political landscape wrought by the “blue wave” of Democratic victories that swept the U.S. midterms. Huang, now aligned with Trump, will face increased scrutiny from congressional Democrats — starting with a public Senate appearance scheduled for next week. He is also expected to testify privately before several House committees next month, including the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

If initial responses from current political leaders are any indication, Huang has his work cut out for him. As news of his return broke on Monday, politicians and public figures from across the political spectrum weighed in — and many didn’t seem too pleased.

articles.headline: Grand Theft Auto 6′s Yard Sales Are Home To Some Amazing Cheap Finds
keyFacts: I walk around most days in brightly colored cordoroy overalls or long skirts and sweaters.
But I know enough to know that Jason Duval has absolutely none of what I think people refer to as “drip.” Guy can’t dress.

body: Look, I don’t know much about fashion. I walk around most days in brightly colored cordoroy overalls or long skirts and sweaters. But I know enough to know that Jason Duval has absolutely none of what I think people refer to as “drip.” Guy can’t dress.

At the start of the game, his closet is depresso mcspresso. Cargo shorts, some faded jeans, the crappiest old T-shirts you’ve ever seen, a couple of okay Hawaiian shirts, and a single plaid flannel that I assume he wears for “special occasions,” like picking up his girlfriend from jail. Awful.

I really love dressing up characters in games and had seen some of the sick outfits you can eventually put Jason and Lucia in later on, so I made it one of my early goals to get the boy something decent to wear. Unfortunately, unless you can rack up a lot of cash and venture pretty far afield, you won’t find too many fashion gems in the early game. The Keys are mostly full of souvenir shops with godawful tourist junk, plasticky sunglasses and ugly shirts and stupid hats. I did find this one pretty sick Vice City tank top and hat in one place, but otherwise the offerings were pretty barren without spending money I didn’t have and desperately needed.
Fortunately, I discovered another option: yard sales.

My favorite thing about GTA VI‘s yard sales is probably finding them in the first place. I’ve complained elsewhere about how small and unreadable Leonida’s road signage is, so trying to spot a tiny “Yard Sale” sign with an arrow is a challenge in and of itself. You can see them on main roads, often on medians, stuck underneath other, more important road signs. When you do find these signs, you have to follow them, but Leonida’s roadways aren’t always clear. I once ended up in a back lot with a bunch of really angry assholes while trying to find a yard sale, and another time I drove into an empty field. Hot tip: yard sales are usually in neighborhoods with yards.

Once you do find the yard sale, you should buy everything there, every time. I always do. For one, it’s all dirt cheap. Single digit numbers of dollars a lot of the time. And it’s all usually cool, and sometimes rare and unique. An easy-to-find early yard sale in Jason’s own neighborhood had one of the sickest T-shirts I’ve ever seen for sale, and also let me pet an alligator that was wearing a cowboy hat.

Speaking of cowboy hats, I followed signs in Gellhorn in Chapter 2 to a different yard sale, where I bought a cowboy hat that I’m told is Arthur Morgan’s and a Hawaiian shirt with cows on it. Later, a guy who was chasing his cow through a field complimented me on my cow shirt, saying he had one just like it. I then went on a crime spree wearing it. Now I’m the Cow Shirt Bandit. I’m unstoppable.

I know Jason and Lucia have their sights set on Vice City, which is a ritzier part of Leonida that will almost certainly have fewer yard sales. So while I’m out in the poorer counties, I’m going to enjoy the thrill of yard sale-ing for as long as I can. Outfits like these are sure to make me a huge hit at all the big yacht parties to come. By the time I make it to the top, Jason and Lucia will be fashion icons, mark my words.

keyFacts: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers.

body: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers.

CVE-2026-76466 , which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services.
The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments.

“An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.”
At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability.

That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available.

“The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.”

Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information.
The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6.
The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices.
A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday.

Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

articles.headline: How to save your Google Nest app videos before the January shutdown
keyFacts: ZDNET’s key takeaways - The Nest app is shutting down on Jan.
- Users who haven’t migrated to the Google Home app still have time to migrate.
- Aside from the Nest app, Google is retiring Google Assistant from speakers and smart displays.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- The Nest app is shutting down on Jan. 25, 2027.
- Users who haven’t migrated to the Google Home app still have time to migrate.
- Aside from the Nest app, Google is retiring Google Assistant from speakers and smart displays.

Google is retiring the Nest app and the site Home.Nest.com on Jan. 25, 2027. If you’re a Nest app user and haven’t migrated to the Google Home app, you should check for unmigrated data before deletions begin on March 25, 2027.

Nest app users who started using the Nest app after Aug. 19, 2019, are likely signed in with a Google Account. You’ll be able to switch directly from the Nest app to the Google Home app once the Nest app shuts down.
More from ZDNET

However, you should know that videos saved in the Nest web clip library won’t transfer automatically to Google Home. Because of this, you should download clips you’d like to keep before the Jan. 25 cutoff. You can use the Download All option in the web clip library.

Aside from manually saving your clips, the biggest issue with the Nest app shutting down is for those who haven’t linked the Nest app to their Google Accounts. Google began prompting existing users to link to their Google Accounts from the Nest app after 2019, while new users were directed to sign up with a Google Account.
How to migrate from the Nest app to Google Home

Unmigrated Nest accounts must be linked to their Google Account soon, as data deletion will begin on March 25, 2027. You can migrate an existing Nest account to a Google Account by following these steps:
- Ensure you have the latest Nest app update for Android or iOS.
- Sign in with your Nest account. To confirm you’re signed into your Nest account, open your Settings and go to Account.
- Within the Account option in Settings, select Migrate to a Google account.
- Tap on Continue with Google.
- Choose the Google Account you use for Google Home, then select Allow to give the Nest app access.
- Review your home members for your smart home.
- Select Complete Migration and follow the prompts to finish.
Keep in mind that some home members may lose access to the Google Home account once your data is migrated, and may need to be reinvited to the Home.
What to do next in Google Home

After you migrate your Nest account to use with Google Home, you can sign in to the Google Home app. You’ll be able to see your devices in Google Home after Jan. 25, though you can also transfer them earlier by accessing the device settings in Google Home.
You should choose Sign in with Google going forward to access your migrated data in Google Home.
Nest Aware subscription plans transition to Google Home Premium and Google Home Premium Advanced plans starting in Jan. 2027.
The end of Google Assistant

Google is retiring Google Assistant from smart speakers and displays in favor of Gemini for Home. The full switch is happening in Aug. 2027, when Google Assistant will be removed from these devices and replaced with Gemini.

Google Home users have been able to opt in to use Gemini for Home since its rollout on smart speakers and displays like the Nest Audio, Nest Mini, and Nest Hub Max. Those who haven’t opted in will no longer be able to keep Google Assistant after Aug. 2, 2027.
Powered by generative AI, Gemini for Home understands more natural phrasing than the rigid commands necessary to speak to Google Assistant.

articles.headline: 'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?
keyFacts: - Published Manchester United's Premier League trip to Anfield was described by some as a free hit for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

body: - Published
Manchester United's Premier League trip to Anfield was described by some as a free hit for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.
The theory was expectations for United were so low as they travelled to Liverpool that a positive outcome would be a huge bonus, and anything else was expected.
But Pochettino did not look like a man without pressure after 15 minutes of what turned into a 4-0 defeat.

By that point, his side were already 2-0 behind and down to 10 men. Liverpool's fans were gleefully singing about the Argentine being "sacked in the morning", even though he was only a sixth of the way through his first game in charge.
A day later, United supporters began filtering through Manchester Airport on their way to Lisbon for a Champions League match that marks the next stop in what has turned into a desperate campaign.
The prevailing mood was one of resigned acceptance punctuated by dark humour around what a season in the Championship might look like, and whether Manchester City might be there with them.
United's England midfielder Kobbie Mainoo summed the situation up when he spoke to MUTV after the final whistle at Anfield.
"We're at the lowest we've ever been and no-one's coming to save us," said the 21-year-old.
"There are no helping hands coming, so we've got to work together, lean on each other, keep working and hopefully it will come good.
"It's all about character now."
Tough tests before the transfer window opens
United are giving little away about their plans for the January transfer window.
For now, it is being stressed, Pochettino's priority is to get the most from the players currently at his disposal.
However, there was sympathy with former boss Michael Carrick's belief he had been let down in the summer window and there was a plan to address that.

That situation remains. A striker is thought to be Pochettino's priority given United's only recognised number nine, Benjamin Sesko, is out at least until January with a shin issue that has bothered him since March.

United have a long-standing issue at left-back. First choice Luke Shaw missed his eighth successive game on Sunday and the only other orthodox left-back in senior ranks is England Under-20 international Harry Amass, who didn't even make the bench at Anfield.
However, Pochettino worked with Shaw at the start of his career at Southampton and feels the 31-year-old can be a positive influence on his group.
The reality though is United still have nine games to play before they can make any changes to their squad.
Among those fixtures are home games against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland.
Newly promoted Coventry are four points ahead of United, who are second from bottom. Forest and Sunderland are in the two positions immediately above the Old Trafford outfit.
A trip to Crystal Palace - the one side below United, and the other Premier League club to replace their coach during the international break - looms on 13 December.
After Wednesday's encounter with Sporting, Pochettino's side have one Champions League game before the end of the year - against RB Leipzig on 8 December.

Any solutions to be found to the current mess over the next five weeks have to come from within. If they don't, light-hearted discussions about a first relegation since 1973-74 under Tommy Docherty start to get serious.
"They have got enough in that squad to get themselves out of the bottom three," Ashley Young - a Premier League winner with United - told Match of the Day.

"They have not been showing that, but Pochettino has only just come in. He is going to want to get his team set up in a way that they are hard to beat. Right now, they do not look like they are hard to beat.
"It doesn't look like there is that togetherness. He has got to find a way to get that out of them. I am sure he will be able to do that when he has been longer in the job."
Fixing a leaky defence
Pochettino shut down a question about United's terrible recent defensive record when he spoke to the media immediately after the game at Anfield.
"Tell me only about the circumstance today," he said. "I wasn't [here] in the past."
That is true - and may also have been a useful diversion exercise in avoiding a dissection of a defensive unit he is still getting to know.

However, Pochettino knows United have kept one clean sheet all season - against Azerbaijani champions Sabah FK in September. He will also know United have now conceded 19 goals in their past six games.
Pochettino's big decision at Liverpool was to pick Matthijs de Ligt in the centre of a three-man defence ahead of Harry Maguire.
"He played in the Champions League you know, before the internationals," said the former Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea boss.
It was not clear when Pochettino meant.

In the 4-1 loss at Como on 21 October, De Ligt made his first appearance in 11 months following major back problems that eventually required surgery, largely because Leny Yoro was suspended and Lisandro Martinez was injured. He then played for two minutes against Roma on 3 November, when he was thrown on as then manager Carrick searched desperately for a winner.
Most goals can be broken down into a number of mistakes that compound to make an eventual negative outcome.

Team positioning has been mentioned as a reason De Ligt found himself exposed under a high ball at Anfield. However, his failure to deal with it presented Alexander Isak with a clear run at goal and prompted Yoro to make the tackle that led to his controversial dismissal, which Pochettino felt shaped the 82 minutes that followed.
But United have been conceding bad goals all season. Numerous players have been culpable.
There is a limit to what Pochettino can do in the time available. However, he wants to maximise what he can do.
Whereas Carrick tended to let his starting players have a day off after matches, the new regime has decided a warm-down session at Carrington is the better option.
And defensive organisation was surely one of the key points his coaching team had on their list of things to work on when the players began preparations to face Sporting on Wednesday.
Will January be the answer Man Utd need?

With Â£70m summer arrival Carlos Baleba injured for the second time since the start of pre-season, Pochettino must find a way to protect United's goal, which might require additional support in midfield.

The strengths of Mainoo and Youri Tielemans are with the ball. Either with three in the middle of defence or a third man in midfield, a way needs to be found to stop opposition attacks running straight at the defence.

In his recent interview with Sky Sports, United chief executive Omar Berrada said the club needed to be "disciplined" in the transfer market and avoid spending huge sums on players who would not necessarily make the squad better.

But the fact former Chelsea midfielder Andrey Santos went five games between Premier League starts under Carrick from the opening-day defeat at Hull - and was only introduced for the final three minutes at Anfield - suggests there are doubts over the Brazilian, who cost Â£48m in the summer.

Underneath that is the knowledge United borrowed from their revolving credit facility around all their major summer purchases and did the same again earlier this month when Pochettino was hired at a cost of just over Â£7.5m.
In public accounts released last week, United confirmed there was another Â£160m available in credit - but also they owe Â£417m in outstanding transfer fees, Â£236m of which is due within 12 months.
Neither before nor after the transfer window opens do any simple solutions to United's predicament present themselves.
Last season, fellow 'big-six' club Tottenham did not save themselves until the final day of the season.
Confidence remains high at Old Trafford the situation will not be quite so dire for them, but it could be a very bumpy ride.

body: Former Rep. Beto O’Rourke (D-Texas) emphasized he believed it was “only a matter of time and effort” before Texas would go blue, just as it did with the midterm elections earlier this month.

O’Rourke — who captured national attention in 2018 when he challenged Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), falling by less than 215,000 votes — appeared on MeidasTouch’s “On Sunday With Jack Cocchiarella” to stress that the flip couldn’t have been about him or anyone else: “It had to be about Texas winning.”

“So, yes, it’s incredibly fucking gratifying and fulfilling to just be a Texan and be an American at a time when the open question was, do we want this corruption and authoritarianism and this oligarchy that is dominating and effectively ruling our country? Or are we capable of something better?” he said.
“Will we meet this challenge the way we did against the British 250 years ago or the Confederacy or the Nazis or Jim Crow? Are we going to overcome these challenges and these odds?”
“And for America to have overcome and to be led by Texas of all places, there’s just some beautiful, poetic political justice in all of this,” he added.

After Sen.-elect James Talarico’s (D) and Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa’s (D) historic wins in Texas, O’Rourke has been praised for his role in getting the ball rolling for Democrats in the Lone Star State, including through his 2022 gubernatorial bid against Gov. Greg Abbott (R).

Moments later, O’Rourke told Cocchiarella that Democrats’ work “has to continue” beyond Election Day, noting that his “biggest mistake” in politics was thinking he could kick back and watch Barack Obama “save the world” when he was elected president in 2008.
“It’s when we place these people in power that they need us more than ever,” he said.

O’Rourke — when asked earlier in the interview about the moment when the “butterflies” went away about this year’s statewide elections — said he held on to his belief in Texas voters, noting that the last two statewide Democratic victories before earlier this month were in 1988 and 1990.

“We are so much better. We’re much bigger, more beautiful people than what you would have reflected in Greg Abbott or Ted Cruz or Ken Paxton or any of these folks who are almost cartoonishly cruel and incompetent and corrupt. That is not Texas. That is just not who we are,” O’Rourke said.
“And my theory of the case has always been that if more people, especially more young people, voted in our elections, we would have better outcomes.”

The party has officially won the largest majority in Congress since the early 1990s. Take a look at NPR's breakdown of the U.S. House races, by the numbers.

Artificial intelligence is causing significant swings in the stock market as investors speculate about the future of the technology boom. While AI stocks have driven markets to record highs and bolstered the economy, concerns are growing about a potential bubble. Investors anticipated that AI giant Anthropic's stock market debut last week would lift markets, but instead Wall Street experienced one of its worst weeks in recent times.

- 🎧 The National Association for Business Economics released a survey asking firms about their AI experiences. NPR's Scott Horsley tells Up First that one in five reported measurable, widespread productivity gains, while about half said they saw some gains, but they weren't widespread. About 30% were either not using AI or felt it was too soon to assess its impact. Austan Goolsbee, head of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, pointed out that the significant investment in AI is already affecting the economy, contributing to inflation by increasing demand for construction materials and electronic components. Although proponents believe AI could eventually help lower costs and limit inflation, Goolsbee tells Horsley that the Federal Reserve must address inflation challenges right now.

Poland has called an emergency NATO session for today after Russia fired three cruise missiles into its territory. The incident highlights the stakes for European countries in Russia's war on Ukraine, prompting nations along NATO's eastern border to seek enhanced air defense support. Poland plans to present proposals to increase surveillance capabilities and deploy more F-35s to intercept incoming missiles and drones.

- 🎧 Anti-missile systems and NATO flights were activated successfully, but Polish authorities say that poor weather prevented them from intercepting the incoming Russian missiles, according to reporter Teri Schultz. No injuries or damage were reported. More than a year ago, NATO established the Eastern Sentry to enhance air defense after a significant drone swarm from Russia entered Poland. Experts are now scrutinizing potential gaps in this defense. If this attack was deliberate by Moscow, Russia is risking severe consequences by endangering the lives of people on the ground in a NATO country, Schultz says.

Delegates at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, couldn't agree on a plan over the weekend to address fossil fuels, the main cause of climate change. The event ran two days longer than expected, making it the longest in the history of these summits. Nearly 200 nations failed to finalize targets for electrification and financial aid for developing countries, or to address the impacts of climate change. The European Union rejected any conclusion that didn't advocate for a transition away from fossil fuels, while oil-producing countries like Saudi Arabia opposed this position. Fossil fuels contribute about 73% of global emissions.

- 🎧 Ultimately, the EU decided that no COP deal was better than a deal that didn't address fossil fuels, NPR's Rachel Waldholz says. She adds that money was another major issue. Developing nations sought increased support to tackle climate change, noting that they've contributed very little to climate change but often deal with the worst impacts. Wealthy nations agreed to provide funding under the Paris Climate Agreement. The U.S. was absent from the discussions due to the Trump administration's withdrawal from international climate negotiations. Many smaller and developing nations are strong defenders of these talks, viewing them as a vital platform to ensure their voices are heard alongside larger countries, Waldholz says.

Behind the story
by Maria Godoy, senior science and health editor and correspondent

People had warned me it might be tough to get Amish people to talk to me as a journalist — and probably impossible to get their permission to record their voice. Not a great omen for compelling radio storytelling.

Yet as I headed off to Lancaster County, Pa., last month to report on the biggest and deadliest measles outbreak in the U.S. in decades, I knew I wanted to hear directly from the community hit hardest.

So I turned to some good old shoe-leather reporting. My producer and I mapped out Amish-owned businesses in and around Lancaster County and spent a day driving around from shop to shop. At every stop, we introduced ourselves and explained the focus of our story. We asked Amish people (easily identifiable by their traditional dress) about their views on the measles outbreak and vaccination. While some declined to talk, others opened up about how measles had affected their families and communities, and why they had or hadn't decided to get vaccinated. To my surprise, one woman even let me record her voice.

Outside a farm supply store in a rural town, I met an Amish woman who was visibly pregnant. Measles can have devastating consequences during pregnancy. She told me her husband and two children had gotten vaccinated to protect her and her unborn child. She declined to give me her name at first, then got in a car driven by her hired non-Amish driver. As they exited the parking lot, the driver stopped to ask us what media outlet we were with. "Oh, NPR!" the driver said when we replied. Then she turned to her Amish passenger and told her, "Don't worry, you can trust them."

Part of gaining trust is about showing up, showing respect and really listening. Word gets around that you're trustworthy. Public health officials in Pennsylvania have also been using a similar approach to win the trust of Amish people as they seek to boost vaccination rates in the current outbreak. You can read more about it here.
